Definition: from a compound of G2556 and G3806; hardship:--suffering affliction.
BiblicalUsage: Kakopatheia is hardship itself — suffering affliction, the lot of the prophets. James holds them up as the example: take the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that affliction is not a sign God has left us; the prophets suffered it and are called blessed, and patience in it is the proof of faith.
